mainTopic: The size of a מקוה, whether the שולחן came apart, and why the four cups at the סדר are not a dangerous pair (זוגות)
overview: This amud opens at the end of a teaching about the size of a מקוה: one אמה by one אמה, three אמות high, which holds forty סאה. רב אשי reports that רבין בר חיננא proved the שולחן in the מקדש was built from detachable parts, because a whole table could not fit into such a small מקוה. The גמרא rejects this proof. Maybe they immersed the table in the huge ים של שלמה, which רבי חייא says held 150 מקואות. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rule that even a poor person gets at least four cups of wine. It asks how חכמים could require this, since a ברייתא warns that doing things in pairs (זוגות) is dangerous. רב נחמן answers that ליל פסח is ליל שמורים, a night protected from harmful forces. רבא answers that the כוס של ברכה counts toward the מצוה but not toward a dangerous pair. רבינא begins a third answer: each cup is its own separate act of freedom, and his sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: The size of a מקוה: one by one by three אמות, forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: The end of a teaching gives the shape of a kosher מקוה and says that this volume equals forty סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A space one אמה by one אמה, three אמות high. The חכמים measured that the water needed for a מקוה is forty סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud begins in the middle of a teaching that defines how big a מקוה must be. It gives the shape (1×1×3 אמות) and the matching volume (forty סאה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line comes from a discussion of measurements that started on the previous amud. It ties a physical shape to a volume, which tells us how big a minimum מקוה is. That size becomes the basis for the next step's question about immersing the שולחן.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of roughly one and a half to two feet
At a height of
The חכמים measured or estimated
A ritual bath used for purification
A measure of volume; forty of them is the minimum for a מקוה

steps.whyThisMatters: The small size of a minimum מקוה (just 1×1 אמה wide) is exactly what makes רבין בר חיננא's argument in the next step possible.

phrases.aramaic: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה בְּרוּם שָׁלֹשׁ אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: A cubit by a cubit, at a height of three cubits,
the measure of the water of a ritual bath as forty se'ah.
phrases.notes: This is the standard source showing that a 1×1×3 אמה space equals forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשִׁיעֲרוּ חֲכָמִים שִׁיעוּר מֵי מִקְוֶה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a discussion of measurements on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מקוה must be at least 1×1×3 אמות, which equals forty סאה.

steps.title: The Temple table was made of detachable parts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רבין בר חיננא told him the שולחן in the מקדש was built from parts that could be taken apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: רבין בר חיננא told me that the שולחן of the מקדש was made of separate parts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought, linked to the topic of measurements. The claim is that the שולחן (the table for the לחם הפנים) could be taken apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is about how the שולחן was built: separate pieces, not one fixed unit. The reason for this claim comes in the very next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The table in the Temple that held the showbread
Made of parts that come apart
Was

phrases.english: Ravin bar Ḥinnana said to me:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אָמַר לִי רָבִין בַּר חִינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the theme of measurements (מקוה size) to make a claim about the שולחן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שולחן of the מקדש was built of detachable parts.

steps.title: Proof: a solid שולחן could not fit into a one-אמה מקוה
steps.stepSummary: If the שולחן were one solid piece, it could not be immersed in a מקוה only one אמה wide, so it must have come apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you thought the table was firmly joined together, how could they immerse it in a space of one אמה by one אמה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין בר חיננא gives his proof. A solid table is too big for a minimum מקוה, so it must have been taken apart to be immersed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שולחן was two אמות long, one אמה wide and one and a half אמות high. A minimum מקוה is only one אמה by one אמה wide (Step 1), so the whole table cannot fit in any direction. If it ever became טמא and needed טבילה, it had to come apart, which proves it was built of parts.

keyTerms.meaning: For if it would enter your mind (if you thought)
It was firmly fastened together
How
Would they immerse it

phrases.english: for if it should enter your mind
that it was firmly fastened together,
how could they immerse it in a cubit by a cubit?!
phrases.notes: The שולחן is 2×1×1.5 אמות; a minimum מקוה is only 1×1 wide.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ הַדּוֹקֵי הֲוָה מִיהַדַּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the claim in Step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the שולחן was made of parts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The minimum מקוה size (1×1×3 אמות) is too small for a whole שולחן.

steps.title: Rejection: maybe they immersed it in the huge ים של שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: there is no real difficulty, because they could have immersed the whole table in the ים של שלמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difficulty? Maybe they immersed it in the Sea that שלמה made.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 3. It suggests a much bigger מקוה where a whole table would fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the table had to be immersed in a minimum-sized מקוה. The גמרא points out that a far larger body of water was available in the מקדש, the ים של שלמה. So the table's size proves nothing about whether it came apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difficulty? (the problem is not real)
Perhaps
The large water basin (Sea) that שלמה המלך built

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not prove the table was solid. It only shows that רבין בר חיננא's proof does not work. The table might still have come apart; we just cannot prove it this way.

phrases.english: Perhaps in the Sea that Solomon made

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not necessarily the claim that the table had parts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed only a minimum-sized מקוה was available; the ים של שלמה was large enough for the whole table.

steps.title: רבי חייא: the ים של שלמה held 150 מקואות
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא's ברייתא shows the ים של שלמה was huge, which supports the rejection.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: the Sea that שלמה made held as much as one hundred and fifty מקואות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection with a source. It shows the ים של שלמה was big enough to immerse even a large table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One מקוה is forty סאה, so 150 מקואות is a huge amount of water. That makes the suggestion in Step 4 realistic, and the proof from the table's size falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: As was taught (in a ברייתא)
Holds, contains
A purification bath (one full מקוה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבין בר חיננא tried to prove the שולחן came apart, because it could not fit in a small מקוה. The גמרא answered that it could have been immersed in the giant ים של שלמה, which held 150 מקואות.

phrases.english: held one hundred and fifty purification baths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that the שולחן was immersed in the ים של שלמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חייא: the Sea held 150 מקואות.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a poor person gets at least four cups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that even a poor person must be given no fewer than four cups of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: they should not give him fewer than four cups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the rule about four cups for the poor at the סדר. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires that even a poor person supported by צדקה get at least four cups of wine for פסח. Quoting this line is a setup: the גמרא is about to ask whether four cups, an even number, is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: And they should not give him less
Than four (cups of wine)

phrases.english: And they should not give him fewer than four.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about the four cups for a poor person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of measurements and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a poor person must receive at least four cups of wine.

steps.title: Challenge: four cups is a pair, and pairs are dangerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how חכמים could require four cups when a ברייתא warns against doing things in pairs (זוגות).
steps.simpleTranslation: How could the חכמים set up something that brings a person into danger? A ברייתא teaches: a person should not eat in pairs, drink in pairs, wipe himself in pairs, or take care of his needs in pairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule of four cups. Four is an even number, made of pairs, and a ברייתא says pairs are dangerous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל held that doing things in even numbers (זוגות) exposes a person to harm from שדים or כישוף. Four cups is two pairs, so the משנה seems to require a dangerous practice. The גמרא asks how חכמים could set up a מצוה that puts people at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים enact or establish
Danger
But wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)? (introduces a challenge)
Two, pairs
Wipe himself

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not drinking too much wine. The problem is the even number: four is made of pairs (זוגות), which חז"ל considered dangerous.

phrases.english: something through which one comes to danger?
A person should not eat pairs,
and should not wipe himself with pairs,
and should not attend to his needs in pairs?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי מְתַקְּנִי רַבָּנַן מִידֵּי דְּאָתֵי בֵּהּ לִידֵי סַכָּנָה, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule quoted in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of four cups of wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Four cups is an even number (pairs), and a ברייתא warns that pairs bring danger, so חכמים should not have required it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the גמרא's famous discussion of זוגות and leads to the idea of ליל שימורים, a night protected from harm.

steps.title: ליל פסח is a protected night
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers the זוגות question from a פסוק. ליל פסח is called ליל שמורים, a night guarded from מזיקין, so pairs are not dangerous on this night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The פסוק says 'ליל שמורים', a night of watching. This means it is a night that has always been guarded from harmful forces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question of how חכמים could require four cups when pairs are dangerous. רב נחמן says the danger simply does not exist on this night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger of זוגות comes from מזיקין, which are harmful spiritual forces. The פסוק calls פסח night 'ליל שמורים', and רב נחמן reads this as a night protected from those forces. Since nothing harmful is active, an even number of cups causes no risk.

keyTerms.meaning: A night of watching (שמות יב:מב), meaning a protected night
Has been guarded all along, from long ago until now
Harmful forces, such as demons, that the danger of זוגות is connected to
The פסוק says. This introduces a proof from a verse.

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea, that ליל פסח is ליל שמורים, is also the source for the custom many have of shortening קריאת שמע על המטה on this night.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: The verse says:

phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות יב:מב.

phrases.english: a night that has always been guarded from harmful forces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of Step 7 about זוגות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the cause of the danger. On this night, the danger itself does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four cups form pairs and should be dangerous, as they would be on any other night.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח night is protected from מזיקין, so pairs pose no danger.

steps.title: The cup of Grace counts for the good but not for the bad
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. The כוס של ברכה, which is the cup of ברכת המזון, joins the other cups to make four for the מצוה. It does not join them to make a dangerous pair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The cup of blessing joins the others for the good, to complete the מצוה of four cups. It does not join them for the bad, to create a pair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer to the זוגות question. רבא admits that pairs can be dangerous, but he says the כוס של ברכה (the cup of ברכת המזון) does not count toward the danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said there is no danger at all. רבא instead says the count never reaches an even number for danger purposes. The כוס של ברכה is a מצוה cup of its own, so it counts toward the four cups but not toward pairs. For the danger, it is as if you only drank three.

keyTerms.meaning: The cup of blessing, the cup used for ברכת המזון
Joins or combines to make a count
For the good, meaning toward the מצוה
For the bad, meaning toward the danger of pairs

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the כוס של ברכה doesn't count at all. It fully counts toward the מצוה of ארבע כוסות. It only does not count toward forming a dangerous pair. Note that the כוס של ברכה is the third cup, the one for ברכת המזון, not the last cup.

phrases.english: and does not combine for the bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כּוֹס שֶׁל בְּרָכָה מִצְטָרֵף לְטוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same קשיא, instead of relying on רב נחמן's protected-night idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the count. One cup is counted for the מצוה but not for the danger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four cups count equally, so they make two pairs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כוס של ברכה counts only for the good, so the danger count stays at three.

steps.title: Each cup is its own separate act of freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a third answer. חכמים set up four cups as expressions of freedom, and each one is treated separately. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: חכמים instituted four cups as a way of showing freedom. Each and every one (continued on the next amud).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a third answer to the זוגות question, from רבינא. This passage ends mid-sentence, so his main point finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's idea is that the four cups are not one set of drinks that adds up to pairs. Each cup is a separate מצוה of דרך חירות, done in the manner of free people. Since each one stands on its own, they never combine into a pair.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים instituted, meaning a rabbinic enactment
In the manner of freedom, the way free people act
Each and every one
Cups (Aramaic plural)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to why the four cups are not dangerous pairs. רב נחמן: the night is protected. רבא: the כוס של ברכה counts for the מצוה but not toward the danger. רבינא: each cup is a separate מצוה.

phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud: each one is a separate מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: אַרְבָּעָה כָּסֵי תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן דֶּרֶךְ חֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent answer to the קשיא of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the cups. Each cup is its own act, so the cups do not combine into pairs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four cups drunk in one evening add up to pairs.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each cup is a separate מצוה of freedom and does not join with the others (completed on the next amud).
